reports.report: The problem asks for the smallest integer $a$ such that $K_{40}$ can have $a$ edge-disjoint perfect matchings $M_1, \dots, M_a$ removed, leaving a residual graph $G'$ with no perfect matching. In $K_{40}$, every vertex has degree $N-1=39$. Removing $a$ edge-disjoint perfect matchings reduces the degree of every vertex in the remaining graph $G'$ to $39-a$. If $a=38$, $G'$ is 1-regular, meaning it must consist of disjoint edges and thus forms a perfect matching itself, contradicting the condition. If $a=39$, all edges of $K_{40}$ are used in the matchings, leaving $G'$ as the null graph, which clearly has no perfect matching. Since $a=39$ is the maximum possible number of edge-disjoint perfect matchings (1-factorization of $K_{40}$), it is the smallest such integer.
